newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SAVINGS BANK BOARD SACKED, NEW BOSS NAMED.
newsitem.headline: SAVINGS BANK BOARD SACKED, NEW BOSS NAMED.

text.p: Lithuania's state-run Savings bank said that the bank council's meeting decided on Friday to sack the chairman and the whole board of the bank and appointed a new chairman, Romualdas Visokavichius.

"The five-member council of the bank, four of them representing state interests, decided today to sack the seven member board of the bank from July 23," the spokesman for the Savings Bank Arunas Marcinkevichius told Reuters.
"The council appointed Romualdas Visokavichius as new chairman of the bank and a five member board from the same date," Marcinkevichius added.
Romualdas Visokavichius headed the country's central bank in the monetary reform period when the national currency litas was introduced in summer of 1993.
Visokavichius worked most recently as temporary administrator of liquidated Innovation Bank.
Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said last week that changes in the top administration of the Savings bank were needed in an attempt to improve its perfomance.
The state-run bank is the biggest in terms of assets.
It is the only one of the three country's banks which was not slated for privatisation.
The bank posted a 30 million litas net profit in 1996 after huge losses of 39 million litas in 1995.
The bank reported last week a 2.1 million litas net profit for the first five months of the year.
The bank's assets stood at 1.4 billion litas, its loan portfolio was 606 million litas and deposits 1.24 million litas at the end of May.
